quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around a truck or bus where cars cannot be seen.
A roadway with rules about stereo volume.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around a truck or bus where cars cannot be seen.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Cars in these spots cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to make a drowsy driver safe.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the impact if you crash.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
You should drive faster to get through the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: A driver's ability can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires the driver to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness can all impair driving.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will hit the curb.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming road hazards. This sign warns that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: An intermediate license has these driving restrictions:

options.text: The driver must wear a seat belt.
All passengers must wear seat belts.
No driving between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.explanation: Young drivers with an intermediate license cannot drive alone between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m., except to school, work, or in an emergency. The driver and all passengers must wear seat belts.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed through the entire curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Then gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up as you enter makes it hard to control your vehicle.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: Always yield to drivers already on the public road when entering from a driveway or private road. Merge safely when you have a clear opening.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Does not change blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not reduce your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or lower your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming. Get ready to stop completely.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or slippery. Driving too fast on poor roads makes it hard to control your vehicle and stop safely.

questions.question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk of a crash when using which of the following?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous. Even hands-free phones take your attention off the road and increase your risk of a crash.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: To reduce road rage, use your turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave extra time for travel. These habits help prevent conflict on the road.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let following cars pass.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic flow is hazardous. On two-lane roads with cars backing up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive in the right lane only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without sudden stops. This prevents the driver behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your ability to judge speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, blurs your vision, makes you misjudge speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and lowers your inhibitions. It makes you more likely to take risks, not calmer.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must and must not do. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should you do to be ready for anything ahead on the road?

options.text: Look around at the entire road and both sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around at the entire road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous driving situations depends on spotting problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but also scan the entire road and the sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?

options.text: You must slow down and get ready to stop.
You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before going.
You can drive through the intersection if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive through the intersection if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians go first.
